subject: MAP: Performance validation & traffic replay scheduling for ACME
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:02:00Z
Subject: MAP: Performance validation & traffic replay scheduling for ACME

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and the MAP draft attached (ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf). High-level outcome from today: ACME wants a performance validation run (traffic replay) to size a Dedicated pool for production, and to validate latency and cost at peak QPS.

Proposed MAP milestone (performance validation):
- Milestone name: Traffic replay & load validation
- Target close date for milestone: 2027-05-13 (aligned to overall deal close)
- Objective: Validate peak QPS support at 99thpct latency <= 350ms and determine Dedicated capacity sizing
- Dependencies: sample traffic, model variant, expected sequence length distribution, and network egress rules for VPC test

Immediate ask: can you confirm acceptance of the rehearsal windows below and share an infra contact for replay artifacts (traffic samples, service account)?
- Canary window (low risk): 2027-04-21 02:00-06:00 UTC
- Full replay window: 2027-04-22 01:00-05:00 UTC
- Target peak QPS we discussed on call: ~2,000 - 2,200 (please confirm exact expected peak)

Next steps / owners (MAP draft):
- ACME: provide traffic_sample_summary.csv + list of endpoints and SSO/service account (owner: Sara / Michael)
- Redwood SE (Marissa): provide replay_config_v2.yaml and recommended Dedicated pool sizing (owner: Marissa)
- Redwood AE (me): coordinate scheduling, HubSpot updates, and rollout plan (owner: Rishi)

Attached: ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (MAP with milestones + responsibilities). Please reply with confirmed replay windows or suggested alternatives — I’ll then loop in Marissa to finalize sizing and the replay config.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Jones <michael.jones@acme.io>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance validation & traffic replay scheduling for ACME

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear MAP. Confirming we can support the windows you proposed with one small tweak: prefer the canary on 2027-04-21 earlier (01:00-05:00 UTC) and full replay on 2027-04-22 01:00-05:00 UTC.

Quick notes from our infra side:
- Expected peak QPS: 2,200 sustained for short bursts (~10-15 minutes)
- Avg tokens per request: ~65 (median 48), peak token length up to 240
- Typical request concurrency pattern: many short requests during peak, then back to baseline

Looping in Michael (infra) who will provide service account + traffic samples. Attaching the initial traffic_sample_summary.csv.

On replay day we will need a Redwood SE on the call for escalations. Also confirm whether Redwood needs a VPN/VPC peering entry or if test can run over public endpoints.

Best,
Sara Holt
Director, Platform Engineering | ACME Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Holt <sara.holt@acme.io>, Michael Jones <michael.jones@acme.io>

Thanks — quick sizing recommendation and test plan from the SE side. High level: we can cover 2,200 QPS with a small Dedicated pool if we optimize batching and KV cache placement. Rough estimate below is intentionally conservative for safety.

Sizing recommendation (initial):
- Model: acme/gpt-large-tiling-v1 (FP16 / int8 paths available)
- Recommended hardware: 4 x H100 GPUs (2x nodes of 2xH100) — this provides headroom for bursts and better batch packing
- Expected QPS per GPU (conservative): ~600 QPS at avg tokens (65) with optimized batching and continuous KV cache
- Notes on latency: with 2 nodes (4 GPUs) and tuned batching target, we can keep 99p approximate <= 300-350ms during sustained bursts. Will need to limit max batch size to keep p99 within target during peak bursts.

Replay/test plan:
- Canary: 2027-04-21 01:00-05:00 UTC — low-ramp to validate telemetry and network config. Redwood engineer on call: Marissa Cole
- Full replay: 2027-04-22 01:00-05:00 UTC — step-ramp to peak, 10m sustained bursts at 2,200 QPS
- Data & creds required from ACME: traffic_sample_summary.csv (received), service account JSON, list of endpoints + IP allowlist if using VPC peering

Operational requirements / checklist:
- Provide a service account with read access to test endpoints (owner: ACME infra)
- Decide on network path: public endpoint (simpler) vs VPC peering (lower jitter) — ACME to confirm
- Confirm model repository access and exact model tag (acme/gpt-large-tiling-v1:v1.3 preferred)
- Provide expected success criteria for pass/fail (we suggest: p99 <= 350ms, error rate < 0.5% during peak)

I attached a minimal MAP PDF (ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) with the milestone table and a starter replay_config_v2.yaml (stub) to the shared Drive link. If ACME confirms, we can reserve 2-node Dedicated capacity week-of Apr 19 to allow warm-up caching.

Thanks — I’ll update the MAP and HubSpot with these numbers and proposed owners.
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
